sources.title: Columbia University: Mongol unity under Chinggis Khan
sources.note: Direct Asia for Educators scholarly teaching resource: 1206 assembly and Temujin’s leadership. Avoids treating the disputed etymology of Chinggis as a settled literal translation.

sources.title: Columbia University: Organization and military tactics
sources.note: Direct discussion of decimal units and feigned retreat. Describes an organizational pattern, not a claim that all units always had their nominal strength.

sources.title: Columbia University: Three invasions led by Chinggis
sources.note: Direct Three Invasions discussion, Xi Xia, Jin and Central Asian campaign beginning 1219; mass slaughter and prolonged conquest. No numerical death tolls inferred.

sources.title: Columbia University: Expansion under Ögödei
sources.note: Direct account, Ögödei reign 1229 to 1241, Jin defeat 1234, Russia and Caucasus expansion. Avoid geographically overbroad source claim that all land north of Yangtze was conquered by 1234.

sources.title: Columbia University: Division of the Mongol Empire
sources.note: Direct account of succession struggles from 1260 and regional sectors, Ilkhans/Golden Horde conflict. Do not adopt its simplified tribal-loyalty explanation or treat a single date as immediate total separation.

sources.title: Columbia University: Khubilai Khan
sources.note: Direct biography, 1215 to 1294 and role as ruler of China. Used narrowly for 1294 death; not as evidence that all other khans acknowledged him then.

sources.title: William of Rubruck: Account of the Mongols, 1253 to 1255
sources.note: Direct University of Washington edition of Rockhill translation with corrections checked against Jackson and Morgan 1990. Sections Yurts and their furnishings, Kumiss, and duties/washing paragraphs. Eyewitness is a foreign Franciscan with biases; statements are attributed and not universalized. Four passages together remain below 200 words.

sources.title: Columbia University: Sheep and pastoral households
sources.note: Full indexed original and direct scholarly site context: wool felt, dried dung fuel, women and children gathering it, care for newborn lambs. No transfer of modern coal practices to medieval households.

sources.title: Jan Bemmann and colleagues: Karakorum, an imperial city in a non-urban society
sources.note: Direct full archaeological article. Sections 3.2 to 3.4 and 4: craftsmen quarter excavated 2000 to 2005, kilns, vessel repair, imported tableware, coerced migrants, yam routes. One primary work cited for three passages with combined words below 200.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Safe conduct pass, 1993.256
sources.note: Full indexed original catalogue. Late thirteenth century, Yuan dynasty, iron with silver inlay; Phakpa script for Mongolian, openwork filled with silver and reverse inverted. Exact quoted English limited to twelve words.

sources.title: Igor de Rachewiltz: Qan, Qa’an and the seal of Güyüg
sources.note: Direct ANU-hosted scholarly article, East Asian History 43 (2019), reprint of 1983 paper. Seal lines 2 to 4 and paragraph distinguishing genitives, yeke Mongγol ulus-un gloss of the Great Mongol Nation. Exact Roman scholarly transcription, no reconstruction of vertical script.

sources.title: On the founding year of the Great Mongol Nation, Journal of Chinese Humanities (2023)
sources.note: Full indexed publisher text, section 1: 1246 letter to Innocent IV bears Uyghur-Mongolian seal with state name. Study distinguishes 1206 investiture from debated naming date; no claim the phrase was demonstrably coined in 1206.

proposedOverrides.name: Mongol Empire
proposedOverrides.summary: A Mongol imperial coalition joined steppe leadership, vast conquests and connected regional courts; its political unity fractured during the thirteenth century.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Existing indexed identity only. No aliases, no new geometry.
batchIdentityNotes.dates: Index 1206 to 1294. Imported HB geometry includes a 1200 start; public narrative instead anchors leadership in 1206. Endpoint 1294 explained as Khubilai death, not universal fall.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: HB shapes cover eastern Asia only: 1200 to 1279 bbox 86.91,41.20,140.85,59.82; 1234 to 1279 bbox 108.36,38.75,133.71,46.53. Site coarse China seam 1234 to 1271 bbox 88,32.6,135.5,53.5. Western conquests absent. Full decoded evidence in parent folder.
batchIdentityNotes.override: Clear inherited fell and successor links pending phase/target geometry review; clear Abbasid predecessor because 1258 conquest is not a predecessor relationship for the empire founded 1206. No geometry repair claimed.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Güyük 1246 seal, exact phrase preserves -un genitive and scholarly gamma. Translation specifically attributed to de Rachewiltz; vertical script not reconstructed.
